newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Huaneng signs new power deals.
newsitem.headline: China's Huaneng signs new power deals.

text.p: China's biggest power company, Huaneng Group, said on Thursday it signed a deal with two Hong Kong companies, Exxon Energy Ltd and Duke Energy (HK) Ltd to develop, own and operate power projects.
The agreement focuses on greenfield or to-be-constucted projects and expansion of existing power facilities in China, said a joint statement issued in Hong Kong by the three companies.
The companies will explore both coal and natural gas-fired opportunities, it said.
Exxon Energy and Duke Energy have worked together to pursue power development opportunities in China under a joint venture agreement signed in March 1995.
China Huaneng Group is a state-owned enterprise which develops, builds and operates power plants and sells electricity to the country's local provincial power companies.
It has 17,325 megawatts of capacity, representing eight percent of China's installed capacity.
